newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-TROUBLED KLINSMANN TO STAY AT BAYERN FOR REST OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TROUBLED KLINSMANN TO STAY AT BAYERN FOR REST OF SEASON.

text.p: Troubled Germany captain Juergen Klinsmann on Monday ruled out a move from Bayern Munich before the end of the season despite his much-publicised problems at the club.
Klinsmann threatened to leave Bayern before the Bundesliga started a two-month break in December because he was unhappy with the team's defensive tactics and the way he has been treated this season.
But the renowned striker, who scored only five goals in the first half of the season, returned to training on Monday after a holiday in the United States in a better mood.
"I have come here feeling good. I want to win the German championship and the German Cup with Bayern," he said. "Anything else is secondary and old hat."
Klinsmann, 32, has until April to decide whether he wants to stay in Munich next season or leave.
Clubs in England where he was a major success with Tottenham two seasons ago are believed to be interested in signing him.
Bayern are looking more and more likely to lose their talented international wing back Christian Ziege to Italy's AC Milan at the end of the season.
Ziege is said to be taking an intensive course in Italian and has agreed a four-year deal with Milan.
Defender Oliver Kreuzer is also understood to be looking for a move at the end of the season. English clubs have shown interest.
